channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Washington bought the Japanese Yen again without meaning to
item.description: USD/JPY closed Wednesday 0.92% lower just above 158.00, the largest single-session decline since the early-August intervention, and Tokyo did not lift a finger for it.

item.title: Pound Sterling's best level since May was made in Washington
item.description: GBP/USD closed Wednesday 0.53% higher just above 1.3600, its best close in three months, and the United Kingdom inflation report that opened the session had almost nothing to do with it. Sterling spent the London morning up barely twenty pips on the day.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar rallies as Treasury buyback drags US yields
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) rallies against the US Dollar (USD), pushing north of the 0.5930 mark. The move is driven by broad weakness in the Greenback rather than anything out of New Zealand.

item.title: Australia unemployment rate expected to hold at 4.4% in July
item.description: Australia will release the July monthly employment report on Thursday at 01:30 GMT. Ahead of the announcement, analysts anticipate a modest 15K increase in job creation, while the Unemployment Rate is expected to remain steady at 4.4%.

item.title: The Dollar Index answers to the Treasury, not the Fed
item.description: The Dollar Index closed Wednesday 0.86% lower just beneath 98.80, its weakest close since mid-May, and it closed on the session low. The document that did the damage was not a central bank document.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD eyes $67 as US yields slide
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) price reversed course on Wednesday and soared over 5% as US Treasury yields edged lower, following the US Treasury stepping in to cap long-end US bond yields, which had reached levels last seen in 2007.

item.title: Euro surges as traders ignore Fed’s hawkish minutes
item.description: The Euro (EUR) gains over 0.85% against the US Dollar (USD) during the North American session on Wednesday, even though the latest Federal Reserve (Fed) minutes had a hawkish tone, with some participants, along with the three dissenters, suggesting that raising rates could be necessary if the disinf

item.title: Forex Today: US Dollar sinks on Treasury buyback ahead of data-heavy Thursday
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) sold off broadly on Wednesday, sinking below the 99.00s region and holding well under 100.00.

item.title: Silver surges as Treasury buyback plan sinks the US Dollar
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades sharply higher on Wednesday, changing hands near $65.80. The metal is riding a broad rally across precious metals with Gold (XAU/USD) soaring toward $4,500.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Franc tests 100-day SMA as US Dollar tanks
item.description: The USD/CHF pair tumbles nearly 2% on Wednesday as a US Treasury buyback announcement sends the Greenback into a tailspin, while US Treasury yields also dive. The pair trades at 0.7979 after reaching a high of 0.8128.

item.title: Gold rallies as buyback sinks yields despite Fed hawkish minutes
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) rallies during Wednesday’s session after the US Federal Reserve (Fed) released the minutes of its July meeting, in which the US central bank held rates unchanged but not unanimously, with three members dissenting and calling for a rate hike.

item.title: Breaking: FOMC officials acknowledged inflation remained elevated
item.description: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) published the Minutes of the July meeting on Wednesday. "The information available at the time of the meeting indicated that inflation remained elevated.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Positive momentum points to further upside
item.description: AUD/USD holds firm near a two-and-a-half-month high on Wednesday, supported by broad US Dollar (USD) weakness, while technical indicators point to further upside. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 0.7118, up 0.43% on the day, after reaching an intraday high of 0.7129.

item.title: Mexican Peso rallies to two-year high on US Treasury buyback
item.description: The Mexican Peso (MXN) rallies to a two-year high of 16.94 on Wednesday as the US Dollar (USD) weakens amid falling US yields, which retreated after the US Treasury doubled the size of its long-duration bond buyback. The USD/MXN pair trades at 16.95, down 0.27%.

item.title: WTI Oil climbs as US-Iran standoff keeps Middle East supply risks elevated
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) Oil holds firm on Wednesday, hovering near its highest level in more than three weeks as traders balance Middle East supply risks against rising US crude inventories. At the time of writing, the US benchmark trades around $85.20 per barrel, up nearly 1% on the day.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar jumps as falling US yields weigh on the USD
item.description: NZD/USD rises sharply on Wednesday and trades around 0.5930 at the time of writing, up 0.96% on the day. The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) benefits primarily from broad weakness in the US Dollar (USD), as the sharp decline in US Treasury yields reduces the appeal of the Greenback.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average rallies on a bid nobody made
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) trades near 53,600 on Wednesday, more than 230 points and 0.44% higher, and none of that gain is about earnings, growth or the Federal Reserve (Fed).

item.title: EUR/GBP pushes toward two-week high amid cooling UK services inflation
item.description: EUR/GBP trades on the front foot on Wednesday, pushing up to the vicinity of a two-week high near the 0.8570 region as the Euro holds firm against a softer British Pound (GBP). The pair has cleared its recent range after a run of green candles on the 4-hour chart.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: BI holds rates to back IDR – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu writes that Bank Indonesia (BI) kept its benchmark rate at 5.75% for a second month in Acting Governor Destry Damayanti’s first decision.

item.title: British Pound jumps as Treasury buyback weakens the US Dollar
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) climbs against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday as the US Treasury stepped up in the markets to offer liquidity support via a buyback of longer-dated bonds, a day after the US 30-year yield hit its highest level since 2007.

item.title: US 10-year Treasury yield tumbles as Treasury steps in to calm bond market
item.description: The US 10-year Treasury yield declines sharply on Wednesday, trading at 4.651% at the time of writing after reaching an intraday high of 4.712%.

item.title: Japanese Yen advances as falling Treasury yields pressure US Dollar
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) extends its intraday gains on Wednesday as the US Dollar (USD) comes under fresh selling pressure following a sharp decline in longer-term US Treasury yields. At the time of writing, USD/JPY trades around 158.47, its lowest level in more than a week.

item.title: United Kingdom: Energy-driven upside risks – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Sam Cartwright notes United Kingdom (UK) headline inflation rose to 2.9% year-on-year in July, driven mainly by higher household energy bills.

item.title: Thai Baht: Higher commodities threaten Baht stability – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts note that the Bank of Thailand (BoT) is expected to keep its policy rate at 1.0%, seeing it as sufficiently accommodative. USD/THB has consolidated in a 32.90–33.30 range, with rising global commodity prices and foreign outflows posing downside risks for the Baht.

item.title: Gold approaches $4,500 as US Dollar and Treasury yields tumble, FOMC Minutes in focus
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) rallies on Wednesday as a softer US Dollar (USD) and a sharp pullback in long-term US Treasury yields help the metal break above its week-old trading range and climb to its highest level since June 4. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,490, up more than 3.5% on the day.

item.title: Canadian Dollar strengthens as Trump pauses 50% tariffs, Oil prices climb
item.description: USD/CAD declines on Wednesday and trades around 1.3810 at the time of writing, down 0.62% on the day.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA keeps hawkish bias on inflation – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu reports the Reserve Bank of Australia remains concerned about inflation, with Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser saying further rate hikes cannot be ruled out.

item.title: Bank of England: Rate hold baseline with conflict risks – Societe Generale
item.description: Sam Cartwright at Societe Generale argues recent easing in United Kingdom (UK) services inflation and labour market loosening support the Bank of England’s wait-and-see stance. The baseline view is Bank Rate stays at 3.75% through 2026 to restrain underlying inflation.

item.title: United States Dollar Index falls as US Treasury doubles long-dated debt buybacks
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) comes under fresh selling pressure on Wednesday as longer-term US Treasury yields fall sharply following the Treasury Department’s decision to expand its buyback operations.

item.title: South Korean Won: Growth-driven recovery offers policy lesson – ING
item.description: Chris Turner at ING explains that Korea’s earlier massive portfolio outflows and a weaker Korean Won (KRW) pushed USD/KRW to 1560 in June, despite a large current account surplus.
